subject: Execution sites, subprocessors, and cross-border transfer — prospect Q&A
messages:
From: Sam Green <sam.green@cardinaltx.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2028-08-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Quick Q: where does our inference data actually run?

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. Before we proceed internally, security asked for a clear, plain-language answer to two things: (1) when we call the Redwood hosted API, in which countries/regions could my request or any derived artifacts be processed or persist (including through subprocessors), and (2) what are the deletion/retention steps — specifically how quickly can we ensure transient request payloads and logs are removed on demand?

I tried to find a simple map but couldn't locate one that lists the cloud partners/subprocessors and whether any handling could cross borders. Can you summarize at a high level and then point us to technical evidence? We may loop in procurement/security later.

Best,
Sam Green
Security Analyst
Cardinal Therapeutics

---

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where does our inference data actually run?

Hi Sam — thanks for the note and great question. I summarized the high-level points below and added Jordan (SE) and Marissa (security) so they can attach the technical map and roster.

High-level summary:
- Primary processing regions: we run customer requests in the region you select (US-West, US-East, EU-West) for Hosted customers.
- Subprocessors: we use a small set of cloud infra providers and a managed logging vendor; those subprocessors are engaged in a limited capacity and we maintain contracts and DPA addenda.
- Cross-border behavior: by default, requests are executed in the chosen region. We do have transient routing for burst capacity and failover that may touch a secondary region; such routing is controlled by policy and can be disabled for customers requiring strict residency.
- Deletion & retention: request payloads are transient (kept in-memory/kv-cache where possible). Durable logs/metrics are retained per your SLA tier; purge-by-request (customer-initiated erase) is supported and typically completed within 48 hours for request payloads, and up to 30 days for residual analytics/log shards depending on archives — we can provide a contractable SLA if you need shorter windows.

I attached a one-page processing locus map and the current subprocessor roster. Jordan and Marissa — could you add more granular evidence (e.g., cloud region mapping, subprocessor roles, and any export-control notes) so Sam has what security needs?

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
kimberly_park@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0132

Subject: Re: Quick Q: where does our inference data actually run?

Hi Sam — Jordan here (SE). Quick technical notes to supplement Kimberly's high-level reply:

1) Execution flow (short):
- API request lands at the regional ingress (customers pick region on provisioning).
- Routing: most requests are pinned to the chosen region; for autoscale/burst we have a policy that allows routing to a pre-authorized secondary region.
- Subprocessor handoffs: persistent storage for model artifacts and logs is provided by CloudStore-A (primary), with a managed logging vendor (LogTraceCo) for long-term metrics. No third-party model providers receive raw customer payloads.

2) Cross-border specifics:
- We do not transfer customer request payloads to partners outside the chosen region except for: (a) controlled failover; (b) support/debug sessions where a customer expressly authorizes remote access; or (c) aggregated telemetry used for platform health (pseudonymized).
- For EU customers wanting zero cross-border transit, we offer region-locking + a dedicated capacity option (Redwood Dedicated) which prevents routing to other regions.

3) Deletion workflow and evidence:
- Transient KV/cache: evicted immediately after session end or on erase request; typical operational window is minutes to hours.
- Durable logs & metrics: we run scheduled compaction and deletion jobs. Erase-by-request for logs is started within 24 hours and completes within 30 days depending on shard topology.
- Evidence we can provide: export of the audit event showing deletion, subprocessor contract excerpts, and a short routing telemetry snapshot for a sample request.

Attachment: subprocessor_roster_aug2028.csv (includes vendor role, region footprint, and DPA link).

If you want, we can provide a sanitized request identifier and walk through its telemetry so your team can see hops.

-Jordan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.ai>
Date: 2028-08-20T10:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Quick Q: where does our inference data actually run?

Hi Sam — Marissa from Security. A few clarifications and commitments from the security/compliance side:

- Subprocessors & contracts: we maintain a POA&M of all subprocessors; the CSV Jordan attached lists the active subprocessors and the minimum contractual safeguards (DPA + standard contractual clauses where applicable).
- Export controls & egress: we have controls to prevent export of data outside customer-authorized regions. For regulated customers we routinely: enable region-locking, disable burst routing, and offer Dedicated or Private deployments.
- Erase request SLA: we are comfortable committing a 48-hour SLA for purge of request payloads and a 30-day contractual window for complete removal of persistent logs for customers on an enterprise contract (shorter windows can be negotiated).
- Evidence pack: we can provide the following on request — subprocessor roster + redacted DPAs, an example deletion audit log (redacted), and a routing telemetry sample. Delivery timeline: ~3 business days for the full pack after a data access request.

If Cardinal requires region-only execution with no cross-border fallback, we recommend Redwood Dedicated in US-West with region-locking toggled on; I can run an impact assessment to estimate cost and latency tradeoffs.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
